setup.welcomeText:
Aqulify adds a real-time 3D acoustic waterfall, a phase and group delay analyzer and an audiophile DSP chain to the Windows audio system (parametric and FIR EQ, crossfeed, partitioned convolver, bass enhancer, limiter).

The installer does everything: it copies the program, adds the plugin to the Equalizer APO chain, creates the shortcuts and adds a proper uninstaller to Programs and Features.
setup.chkApo: Add to the Equalizer APO chain (live DSP + accurate measurement at the end of the chain)
setup.chkDlApo: Download and install Equalizer APO (sourceforge.net, ~12 MB, free)
setup.chkAuto: Start with Windows (in the background, with a tray icon)
setup.chkReboot: Restart the computer now (required to activate Equalizer APO)
setup.apoInstalled:
✔ Equalizer APO installed: {path}
Aqulify goes to the end of the chain, so it measures exactly what goes to the DAC.
setup.apoMissing: ⚠ Equalizer APO is not installed. The installer can download and start its setup; without it, Aqulify only analyzes (the DSP settings do not affect the sound).
setup.noteInstalled: Adding it puts a single line into the EQ APO config.txt (Include: Aqulify.txt); your own filters stay untouched. The uninstaller removes it.
setup.noteMissing: The Equalizer APO installer starts in a separate window: at the end, tick the audio device you listen to music on, then restart the computer when asked.

setup.subWelcome: Phase, spectrum and acoustic waterfall – Windows 11
setup.doneIntegrated: The plugin is in place in the Equalizer APO chain; the waterfall and the DSP work live.
setup.doneAnalyzer: Aqulify runs in analyzer mode (WASAPI loopback). For live DSP, install Equalizer APO, then run this installer again.
setup.doneReboot: Equalizer APO has just been installed: it takes effect on the audio device only after a restart.
setup.doneTray: Aqulify runs in the taskbar (notification area): double-click opens the interface, right-click opens the menu. It is also available from the Start menu.
